terms.gloss: rouge, a dark red face paint

evidence: Plaut. Most. 1.3.118: vetulae, quae vitia corporis fūcō occulunt (Lewis & Short s.v. fūcōsus)
terms.comment: Properly orchil, a red dye from a lichen; then rouge, and figuratively pretence. Lewis & Short prints this word inside the entry for fūcōsus; the separate fūcus is a drone.

sources: Lewis & Short: purpurissum · Lewis & Short: fucus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 372.
